bull.b: Long-term contracts, recurring rent, contractual escalators, and multi-tenancy create durable revenue visibility. Adding tenants or equipment to existing sites can increase revenue with relatively low incremental operating costs, supporting resilient economics over multiple quarters.

High gross and EBITDA profitability is supported by substantial operating and free cash flow, indicating that reported earnings are backed by cash generation. This provides capacity to fund infrastructure investment, service obligations, and maintain capital allocation flexibility.

CoreSite adds a structurally attractive growth engine alongside the tower portfolio. Strong demand from cloud, enterprise, network, and AI customers, combined with pricing power and a large expansion pipeline, can support sustained revenue growth and diversification.

bear.b: Very high leverage leaves AMT more exposed to refinancing costs, interest-rate changes, and reduced financial flexibility than a lower-debt business. Even with strong cash generation, the large debt base can constrain investment, distributions, and responses to operating setbacks.

Reported AFFO growth masks a flatter underlying outlook once DISH churn and refinancing effects are removed. Limited normalized growth over the near term could constrain per-share earnings momentum and makes execution on leasing, services, and financing plans more important.

Brazilian churn is weighing on the international tower portfolio and demonstrates that regional tenant conditions can interrupt otherwise recurring infrastructure revenue. A slower market repair would prolong pressure on organic growth and could reduce the contribution from emerging markets.
